body.x: AJ2 (CEO Gil Soo Jung) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, which opened on January 6 (local time) in Las Vegas.

AJ2 is a security and authentication solutions company specializing in iris recognition–based biometric technologies. Focusing on the iris—known for its higher individual specificity and resistance to forgery compared with fingerprints or facial features—the company has introduced high-reliability authentication solutions applicable across a wide range of environments and industries.

In parallel, AJ2 continues to advance next-generation biometric technologies through sustained R&D, applying AI (artificial intelligence) to maximize recognition accuracy and versatility while strengthening global competitiveness.

At CES 2026, AJ2 unveiled a next-generation iris recognition platform that integrates AI algorithms with dedicated hardware. Having participated in CES since 2023, the company aims to use this year’s exhibition as a turning point to demonstrate the competitiveness and scalability of its technology in global markets and to accelerate ongoing international collaboration efforts.

The iris recognition solution presented at CES is built on AJ2’s proprietary CNN-based deep-learning algorithm, ‘iris,’ achieving recognition accuracy approaching 95 percent. According to the company, this delivers higher reliability and a more stable authentication environment than conventional biometric systems.

The platform also demonstrates strong hardware competitiveness. AJ2 has independently developed core optical components—including high-resolution lenses and infrared (IR) LEDs that effectively suppress light scattering—and tightly integrated them with its software. This approach improves iris image capture quality and focal distance while reducing hardware costs compared with competing products, securing both performance and cost efficiency.

body.cap: A visitor experiences AJ2’s iris recognition solution at the company’s booth. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Notably, AJ2’s iris recognition platform can perform fast, accurate authentication at approximately one meter. By lowering hardware costs relative to competitors, the system combines economic efficiency with robust performance. In addition, enhanced tolerance to environmental variables—such as changes in illumination and user positioning—allows the platform to maintain stable recognition performance even in outdoor settings.

Looking ahead, AJ2 plans to extend the technology to enable stable recognition at distances beyond three meters. The platform is also designed to sustain performance under diverse environmental conditions, further reinforcing its applicability across use cases.

AJ2’s lightweight, modular design ensures compatibility with a wide range of devices. Beyond fixed access-control systems, the technology can be applied to mobile devices, unmanned authentication kiosks, and contactless payment systems. In the healthcare sector, the company also sees potential to develop biomarker technologies that utilize iris data.

Gil Soo Jung, CEO of AJ2, said, “CES 2026 is an important stage to introduce the lightweight design, scalability, and reliability of our iris recognition technology to the global market. We are here to expand our business scope beyond conventional security solutions into mobile biometrics, fintech, and healthcare.”

He added, “The iris is not only far more precise and distinctive than facial features or fingerprints, but also a promising biomarker that can reflect aspects of an individual’s health. AJ2’s technology has the potential to create new value across a wide range of industries beyond security and authentication.”
